scope: Native port with 16 of 102 catalogued games implemented. Migration continues in source-audited batches; the server runs a five-minigame ranked series. Remaining 86 games, boards and original Party modes are not implemented.
sessionBehavior: Server-adapted series of five distinct implemented minigames. Each round votes among unplayed games. Rank points are original player count minus competition rank plus one; equal raw scores get equal rank/points. The final ranking uses the five-round sum, with one match result recorded. Original Quick Play is a single minigame.
knownDifferences: Difficulty selection is not exposed. Normal difficulty is used where source difficulty branches apply: Dropper ring spacing 10+2*min(level,5), red-light reaction window 19 ticks; multiplayer time limits are used.
Same-tick finishes or falls are tied rather than resolved by selector order.
Scene extraction excludes entities and block-entity NBT; original decorative barrel inventories, custom skull textures, banner patterns, sign text and campfire contents are not reproduced.
Nine newer decorative plants in Tile Capture medium are replaced by 1.21.1 counterparts; resource metadata records exact replacements. The 11 phase-2 crops require no additional block substitutions.
Decorative water and lava remain static inside Party scenes to prevent cropped channels from flowing into other arenas.

Disconnecting or leaving before results forfeits this server's match: remove the player from pending rankings and continue, ending when fewer than two remain. Published results are frozen. Original end functions sometimes wait for every participant to reconnect; this port does not.

Runner follows the active source functions: falling colored blocks can damage lower-floor players and are removed after landing; lower oak-plank floors are not destroyed by the falling blocks. The normal 10-tick stillness check is used; the source high-ping 20-tick setting is not exposed.

The new crops omit original NBT for 10 banners in Memory Lane first, 20 signs in Memory Lane second, and 8 banners, 12 signs and 4 campfires in Meat Slap. Generated gameplay labels do not restore these original decorative contents.

Platforms retains the original exactly-four-player constraint and six internal gem rounds; it is offered only while four participants remain eligible. Hidden-round signs are generated with native scoped callbacks instead of copying source run-command click events.

Cave Parkour retains the complete 1,031,051-block cave terrain, 39 checkpoint anchors and a linked random route graph with 22 branches across 11 nodes. Its 28 iron_chain blocks use the 1.21.1 chain name with the same axis and waterlogged properties.

Whack-A-Mob and Monster Shoot use scoped native target subclasses to retain targets on a Peaceful host and suppress original-map-disabled loot and XP, without changing shared-world difficulty, gamerules or ordinary mobs. Scoped explosion and silverfish protections reproduce the original mobGriefing=false behavior.

Native PvP collision is selected per Party round: noncombat games keep the original pvp=false arrow pass-through, while Meat Slap and One Shot Wonder retain player combat. This does not change the shared server PvP setting.

games.name: Whack-A-Mob (WAM)
implementationNotes: Original 90-second normal-difficulty Whack-A-Mob; whack_a_mob_start overrides the entry function's preliminary 1200-tick value with 1800 ticks. A shared 20-tick spawn cycle chooses a weighted type and an empty one of nine holes, mirrored into max(4, initial player count) source rooms.

Native netherite-axe cooldown and damage, iron armor mitigation, health values 10/10/10/9/4/10, Enderman NoAI/hide/reappear and source movement/life rules are retained. Source type weights are zombie 4, wither skeleton 1, armored zombie villager 1, enderman 1, blaze 2 and zombified piglin 2.

Per-type killed statistics award each type once per source tick, even for multiple same-type kills. Points flush before the final alive-target drain check. Retraction /kill does not award specific killed-type statistics without a direct player damage source.

The source keeps the previous hole when all nine are occupied, and excludes Blazes from the ordinary low-Y retraction kill. Unhit Blazes may continue descending until source-world void damage; the game waits for these live targets rather than applying a new timeout. Source Y<-128 void behavior is retained despite arena translation.

The complete ten-room geometry is preserved. Twenty iron_chain blocks use the original 1.21.1 chain name with unchanged axis/waterlogged properties. Fifty decorative pipe signs, twenty decorative skull profiles and nine banner patterns are not reconstructed.

Player environmental damage and generic-kill retries remain enabled; damage from other players is disabled. Retries reset health, fire, hit state and equipment, and apply native respawn protection. Fall damage follows the arena default for this server's five-round adaptation rather than inheriting the original map's preceding mode state.

games.name: Monster Shoot (MSh)
implementationNotes: Original 60-second Monster Shoot with 25 random spawn markers, source type weights zombie 5, creeper 3, silverfish 2 and skeleton 2, and player-count spawn delays 20/17/14/12/10/9/8 ticks for <=4/5/6/7/8/9/10 players.

All targets have five health. Zombies ride invisible five-health chickens; skeletons/zombies wear stone buttons as helmets. Native AI, gravity, slow falling, chicken gliding, passenger motion, collision and ground/orphan cleanup are retained.

The bow retains Power V and Infinity. Actual arrows receive PierceLevel 1, following the source tick rather than the decorative Piercing V enchantment. Points are zombie 1, creeper 2, skeleton 3, silverfish 5 and chicken 1, coalesced once per player/type/source tick.

After 1200 ticks spawning stops and the game waits for no alive monster-tagged target. The source end test runs before pending-stat flush and removes objectives before placements, so pending points on the final drain tick are discarded; corpses do not delay this condition.

Five or more players use the original radius-12 player_circle with integer floor(360/N) yaw increments and centered execute-position coordinates. The complete pit, ledges, bottom introduction position and spawn-height terrain are preserved; twelve decorative banner patterns are omitted.

games.name: Cave Parkour (ACP)
implementationNotes: Original 200-second multiplayer parkour with 15 progression stages and 39 possible checkpoint anchors. A checkpoint requires the original radius and redstone-lamp check; the finish requires the original beacon check.

The 22 original command-block branch chains are converted into ordered typed set/fill/clone data in cave_parkour_routes.json. Only the selected branch successor is visited, preserving linked random routes and terminal shortcuts.

Right-clicking the checkpoint reset item or dying retries from the last saved checkpoint. Source environmental damage, hunger saturation and invisibility are scoped to participants. Ranking combines checkpoint progress with order of reaching that progress.

The 64 original arrow signs and 14 clone-source sign texts are extracted as whitelisted literal strings; native text updates preserve wayfinding without copying click events or arbitrary block-entity NBT.

games.name: Raft Racers (RRs)
implementationNotes: Current source entry uses boat_race_generate_mpm in the End, with four routes 11..14; the obsolete six Overworld routes are preserved only as source hashes. Complete active course is 313x71x383 and is never compressed or folded.

Native bamboo raft, packed-ice physics and bubble columns; sequential source light markers at player Y+10, finish coral at Y-1.5, two laps, 3600 ticks and N-1 finish threshold. Unfinished racers rank by laps times initial count plus original last-lap recency order; intermediate waypoints do not add points.

Owner-scoped recall item works by right-click or drop, with 200-tick cooldown. Native boat/player leash, packed-ice safe marker and below-Y44 replacement follow the source; all boats, rabbits, arrows and tagged drops are scoped and removed on close.

1.21.1 steering requires player as first passenger and invisible source rabbit second. Invulnerable source rafts also suppress legacy 1.21.1 fall destruction while retaining native movement. The source player-10 reset-token mismatch is adapted to UUID ownership.

games.name: Knockout (KO)
implementationNotes: Original multi-level volcanic arena and separate 11x10x11 upper clone, including clone air. Each player has three lives, native Knockback I stick and immediate first-playerKillCount upgrade to Knockback II.

Native getPrimeAdversary supplies kill attribution including recent knockoffs; recycled player entities clear both attacker references on each new life. Feet-in-lava forces death; native environmental damage remains enabled. One randomly chosen pending player respawns per tick at one of nine original markers.

Regeneration amplifier44 refreshes every tick; 300 ticks with no actual damage dealt or taken enables glowing, reset on actual damage. Native 60-tick respawn protection excludes fall and invulnerability-bypassing damage. There is no timer; the final surviving player ends the round.
Death interception reuses the player entity instead of executing original global scoreboard, spawnpoint, team or game-rule commands. Doubles is not exposed in this server free-for-all series.

games.name: Hoopin' n' Swoopin' (SF)
implementationNotes: Original 36-ring descending spiral is rebuilt from literal fill/clone geometry and five air-inclusive ring templates, with exact corner turns, template changes and random offset ranges; saved random holes are not copied.

Native unbreakable Binding Elytra, one attempt, source resistance99 and weakness99. Landing on iron bars or descending to source Y<=-32 removes the Elytra; cached previous-tick Y=-40..-32 suppresses jumping.

Score reads the 37 original floor materials at source Y=-42 under current X/Z, retaining prior score when no material matches. There is no timer; all remaining players must reach the dead-bubble-coral floor detector, and final scores freeze before observer/lobby teleport.
The 1.21.10 iron_chain state is translated to 1.21.1 chain with the same axis and waterlogged properties. Original global schedules, selectors and rules are not executed.

games.name: Meat Slap (MSl)
games.difficultyPolicy: Normal where the source has difficulty branches; fixed source rules otherwise. No difficulty selector or single-player variant is exposed.
implementationNotes: Source Meat Slap is a 120-second tag timer: least time holding the meat wins; holder has Speed IV and Sharpness X porkchop; transfer requires the source 6.5-damage threshold.
The previous holder relocates to an original marker at least 24 blocks from the tagged player. The port pairs attacker and victim within this session instead of using global damage-stat selectors.

If the holder leaves, a remaining player becomes the holder. Out-of-bounds or unexpected death returns to the starting position instead of eliminating the player; this is a same-server recovery adaptation.

games.name: Platforms (Pl)
implementationNotes: Original exactly-four-player game of six internal rounds. Each player chooses left/middle/right, then armor-stand motion carries the player to a target platform. Players reaching the same platform receive no gems.

Outer-platform gem count ranges by internal round: [1,2], [1,2,3], [2,3,4], [2,3,4,5], [3,4,5], [4,5]. The central platform ranges are [3,4], [4,5,6], [5,6,7], [6,7,8], [7,8,9], [8,9]. Each diamond uses one of the original nine markers for that platform.

The last two internal rounds hide players while choosing and use the original twelve sign positions. Native sign text and callbacks replace source command events. Raw minigame score is total gems multiplied by two; the outer five-round series converts the resulting rank to tournament points.

Gem tally preserves platforms_jump3's full-Inventory queries, including offhand: each stack count from 1 through 9 is awarded once when present. Manually splitting gems into duplicate equal-sized stacks does not award that count twice. Dropped diamonds within the original 11-block sphere are cleared between internal rounds.

games.difficultyPolicy: Normal where the source has difficulty branches; fixed source rules otherwise. No difficulty selector or single-player variant is exposed.
implementationNotes: Source 90-second FFA kill contest uses modern sword/bow combat, arrow damage 99, one arrow on spawn and an additional arrow per credited kill. Arrows can accumulate.

Random respawns use the original 24 marker entries, including the repeated marker. Players return on the following tick with a fresh life and the native new-player 60-tick non-fall damage protection; fall and invulnerability-bypassing damage follow the vanilla exception.

The port credits each kill directly; it does not reproduce the source kills2==1 selector edge case that can lose arrow awards for multiple kills in one tick. Dropped/grounded projectiles are removed within the session.
